re_line: Lai's Double Ten speech, militia boat off Taiwan, EU-China hybrid deal, China's Laos base, Webull probe
editors_note: This is the second China Room Brief. It arrives every Tuesday with a recap of the past week in U.S.-China relations and a look ahead.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: House China panel faults Webull over China links
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan Select Committee on China investigation led by Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) found that brokerage Webull Financial "has not been transparent about its links to China." Webull shares fell after the House panel flagged the ties, Reuters reported.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Moolenaar asks Fed to review Hong Kong dollar access
heard_on_the_hill.body: Rep. John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on the CCP, called in a committee release for a review of Hong Kong's access to a Federal Reserve liquidity facility.
heard_on_the_hill.event: Moolenaar Hong Kong Fed facility review

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senators cite FBI spy case as CCP repression in U.S.
heard_on_the_hill.body: Republican Senators Blackburn, Ricketts and Scott called the case of Zhang Wanying, charged with acting as an unregistered PRC agent after allegedly surveilling an adult child of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, evidence the CCP is exporting repressive surveillance to the United States, VOA Chinese reported. China's foreign ministry said it was unaware of the case.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bennet among lawmakers visiting Taiwan after summit
heard_on_the_hill.body: Several U.S. lawmakers are visiting Taiwan following last month's Trump-Xi summit, VOA Chinese reported, with AIT saying the visits reinforce the U.S.-Taiwan partnership. AIT announced that Senator Michael Bennet is visiting this week to meet senior officials on regional security.

in_the_news.headline: Lai says Taiwan will not give up its freedom; Beijing calls him 'pragmatic independence worker'
in_the_news.body: Lai Ching-te told Double Ten crowds in Taipei that Taiwan "cherishes peace" but will not give up its freedom, and pledged a record NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) for defense in 2027, the Washington Post and AFP reported. Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office called him a "pragmatic Taiwan independence worker," and China announced live-fire drills in four seas for October 12-20. Washington welcomed Lai's commitment to Taiwan Strait stability.

in_the_news.event: Chinese militia boat off Taiwan's east coast
in_the_news.headline: China militia boat spotted for first time off Taiwan's east coast
in_the_news.body: A Chinese maritime militia boat, the Minfudingyu 07902, was seen off Taiwan's east coast in mid-August, the first confirmed sighting there, Reuters reported. A State Department spokesperson said China's patrols off the east coast "only exacerbate tensions." Taiwan's defense ministry said Beijing is using "law enforcement and scientific research as cover for harassment" to practice for a potential blockade.

in_the_news.headline: China, EU step back from trade war with limits on hybrid car exports
in_the_news.body: The EU agreed to cap imports of Chinese-made hybrid vehicles at 350,000 units a year after Maroš Šefčovič and Commerce Minister Wang Wentao met in Beijing October 8-9, Bloomberg reported. The EU said the deal could roughly halve such shipments over four years, according to the New York Times. MOFCOM said it secures China's "export space" in Europe.

in_the_news.headline: China expands military reach with new base in Laos
in_the_news.body: China is building a military facility with a new runway at Ban Keun, Laos, the New York Times reported, and neighbors are watching whether Beijing expands it for larger aircraft. Reuters satellite imagery showed attack aircraft and military vehicles at the site. An analysis in The Diplomat disputed calling it an attack base, counting eight Chinese training aircraft at a joint support center that opened September 29.

in_the_news.headline: China nominates health official to lead WHO
in_the_news.body: Beijing has nominated Song Li, a senior official of the All-China Women's Federation, for WHO Director-General, Reuters reported. The Washington Post placed the bid within Beijing's push to fill multilateral leadership gaps amid reduced U.S. engagement with UN institutions.

research_roundup.event: Chinese research vessels and undersea infrastructure
research_roundup.headline: China’s Weaponization of Dual-Use Research Vessels for Undersea Data Dominance
research_roundup.body: Jose M. Macias III, Tao-Hung Chang, Nico Vacca and Benjamin Jensen analyze 223 vessels and find that Chinese research ships spend an unusually large share of time near subsea infrastructure on the high seas. They call for stronger allied monitoring, coordinated patrols and faster cable repair.

research_roundup.event: PLA lessons from Russia-Ukraine drone war
research_roundup.headline: Learning Without Bleeding: China’s Lessons from the Russia-Ukraine Drone War
research_roundup.body: Lilly Min-Chen Lee and Kateryna Bondar trace how quickly Chinese analysts identify battlefield innovations and how the PLA translates them into training, procurement, hardware and force structure.

research_roundup.headline: Russia’s Turn to China Under Sanctions: Sanctions Decay, Substitution Elasticity, and the Challenge of Sustaining Pressure
research_roundup.body: Damien Spleeters argues that sanctions lose force not only when governments stop updating them but also when targeted actors replace restricted products, suppliers and acquisition channels faster than controls can adapt.

research_roundup.headline: Understanding the Chinese-Language Media Landscape in Southeast Asia
research_roundup.body: Lauren Mai, Andreyka Natalegawa, Gregory B. Poling and Japhet Quitzon argue there is no viable strategy for countering Chinese information warfare without buy-in from regional partners and awareness of the scale, scope and impact of Chinese-language media in Southeast Asia.

research_roundup.headline: China's Stealth Support of Iran: A Conversation with Mona Yacoubian
research_roundup.body: Mona Yacoubian discusses the current state of the war in Iran and Beijing's evolving relationship with Tehran.
